summary: Earth System Trend Detective is an interactive 3-page scientific workbench built to help high school students, university researchers, and citizen scientists uncover and verify multi-decade regional environmental trends. Users select any global coordinate or launch one-click regional case studies—such as Winter Solar Dimming & Urban Heat in Lahore, Karakoram Snowpack shifts, Thar Desert Atmospheric Thirst, or Amazon Topsoil Drying—to investigate 9 key variables across four Earth science branches: Atmosphere & Radiation, Hydrosphere & Water Balance, Cryosphere & Soil Systems, and Wind & Boundary Layer. Because strong seasonal swings often obscure long-term environmental shifts, our analytical engine decomposes raw monthly records into deseasonalized signals, rolling long-term trends, recurring seasonal cycles, and residual anomalies. It automatically computes Sen’s slope (annual rate of change with 95% confidence intervals) and executes a non-parametric Seasonal Mann-Kendall significance test (p < 0.05) with plain-English detective conclusions. Featuring decade-by-decade regime shift analytics, a cross-branch Pearson correlation matrix, plain-language variable briefings, and one-click CSV telemetry export, the platform transforms raw Earth observation data into accessible scientific discovery.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS: EARTH SYSTEM TREND DETECTIVE

1. Problem & Motivation

Earth’s environmental systems are constantly changing, yet identifying genuine long-term shifts inside noisy satellite and climate datasets is difficult for students and non-specialists. Global averages often conceal severe regional changes—such as localized droughts, urban heat island intensification, or winter smog dimming—while strong seasonal cycles (summer heat vs. winter cold, or monsoon wet vs. dry seasons) mask gradual multi-decade linear trends. To become true "data detectives," users need a tool that pairs plain-language variable guidance with rigorous statistical significance testing (p < 0.05) rather than relying on visual guesswork.

2. How Our Solution Works

Earth System Trend Detective is a 3-page interactive web workbench built in Python and Streamlit that enables students, educators, and citizen scientists to investigate multi-decade regional environmental trends across the globe:

- Multi-Branch Earth System Catalog (9 Variables across 4 Disciplines):

1) Atmosphere & Radiation: Surface Solar Irradiance (MJ/m²), Daytime Maximum Temperature (°C), Nighttime Minimum Temperature (°C), and Vapor Pressure Deficit (kPa).

2) Hydrosphere & Water Balance: Total Precipitation (mm) and Reference Evapotranspiration (mm).

3) Cryosphere & Soil Systems: Snowfall Accumulation (cm) and Topsoil Moisture 0–7 cm (m³/m³).

4) Wind & Boundary Layer: Maximum Sustained Wind Speed (km/h).

- Guided Regional Case Studies & Plain-Language Briefings:

Every variable includes a clear scientific definition and real-world detective clue. Users can enter any custom latitude and longitude or launch one-click regional hotspots—including Winter Solar Dimming & Urban Heat in Lahore, High-Altitude Snowpack in the Karakoram, Atmospheric Thirst in the Thar Desert, Evapotranspiration in California's Central Valley, and Topsoil Drying in the Amazon Basin.

- Three-Page Interactive Workbench:

* Page 1 — Orbital Trend & Seasonal Decomposition: Separates raw monthly observations (1984–2024) into Deseasonalized Signal, Rolling Long-Term Trend, Recurring Seasonal Cycle, and Irregular Residual Anomalies. Calculates Sen’s Slope (robust annual rate of change with 95% confidence intervals) and executes a non-parametric Seasonal Mann-Kendall Significance Test (p < 0.05), generating an automated plain-English detective conclusion.

* Page 2 — Decade Regime Shift & Anomalies: Visualizes annual departures from the long-term baseline, decade-by-decade distribution statistics (mean, median, min, max from the 1980s to 2020s), and 12-month climatology profiles.

* Page 3 — Cross-Branch System Coupling: Demonstrates physical interactions between Earth’s spheres using a Pearson Correlation Matrix (r), interactive driver-vs.-response scatter plots (such as temperature vs. soil moisture), and one-click CSV data export for further classroom or research analysis.

3. Technical Stack & Scientific References

- Architecture & Tools: Python, Streamlit (Custom Orbital Dark Glassmorphism Interface), NumPy, Pandas, Classical Additive Seasonal Decomposition, OLS 95% Confidence Intervals, and Seasonal Mann-Kendall Non-Parametric Hypothesis Testing.

- Deployment & Code: Publicly hosted on Streamlit Community Cloud with full open-source code and documentation on GitHub.

- NASA & Earth Science Frameworks: Modeled on NASA Earth Science Division variable definitions, NASA POWER / global reanalysis monthly aggregation standards (1984–2024), and CUAHSI hydrological time-series analysis methodologies.
